html:
SMTO-EXE-0088 — The window SMTO wanted to capture is closed or hidden

GUID: 46eff3c4-f004-5c38-aaf5-aa6d3c187fe5
Slug: screen-stale-window
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO tried to capture a window that is closed, minimized or hidden, or there was no window in front to look at. Nothing was captured.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the window you want SMTO to see, make sure it isn't minimized, and click it so it's in front. SMTO captures only visible windows, and some requests use the window you're working in.
  2. Don't move or resize the window while SMTO takes the picture. If the window moves during the capture, SMTO throws the picture away rather than return a mismatched one.
  3. Ask SMTO again to look at that window, so it finds the window as it is now. A window gets a new identity when its app restarts, so SMTO needs to find it again.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns a screenshot or the text of the window you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the name of the app whose window you wanted, to the person who manages that computer. Don't ask SMTO to capture a different computer's screen instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested window_id was not found or not visible, no focused window was reported for screen.context, or the window's bounds changed during a context capture.

What this means

  • A requested window could not be found or was not visible, or screen context required an active window when none was reported. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A requested window could not be found or was not visible, or screen context required an active window when none was reported.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh active-window metadata and inspect current visibility without substituting another application's window.

How to fix it

  • Call screen.active_window again on the same Gateway and use the current visible window_id; window identities end when the window closes or its app restarts. For screen.context, make sure a window is focused and stays still while it is captured, because a bounds change during capture is rejected.
  • Call screen.active_window again on the same Gateway and use the current visible window ID.

Retry and execution caution

  • Call screen.active_window again on the same Gateway and use the current visible window ID.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended visible window resolves to a current identity before capture or OCR.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
